title: GMAT Focus Quant Practice Test 29
instructions: GMAT Focus Edition Quantitative Reasoning: 21 Problem Solving questions, 45 minutes. An on-screen calculator is permitted.

questions.prompt: £240.00 buys items costing £6.00 each. After a 20% price rise, how many fewer whole items does the same money buy?
questions.explanation: At £6.00 the money buys 40 items. After the rise each costs £7.20, and £240.00 / £7.20 is 33.33, so 33 whole items. That is 7 fewer. 33 is the new count rather than the drop, and a 20% rise in price does not mean a 20% fall in what can be bought.

questions.prompt: Solve for the positive value of x: x² = 3x + 28
questions.explanation: Bringing everything to one side gives x² − 3x − 28 = 0, which factorises as (x − 7)(x + 4) = 0 because 7 and -4 multiply to −28 and add to 3. The solutions are 7 and -4, and the positive one is 7. Checking: 7² is 49 and 3 × 7 + 28 is 49.

questions.prompt: Six numbers have a mean of 18. One is removed and the remaining five have a mean of 20. What was the number removed?
questions.explanation: The six total 108 and the five total 100, so the number removed is the difference: 8. Removing a number below the mean must pull the mean up, which is why the answer had to be smaller than 18.

questions.prompt: A rhombus has sides of 13 cm and a perpendicular height of 10 cm. What is its area?
questions.explanation: A rhombus is a parallelogram, so its area is base times height: 13 × 10 = 130 cm². 65 cm² halves it as though it were a triangle, and 169 cm² would be the area if the shape were a square of side 13.

questions.prompt: One person invests twice as much as a second, and the second invests three quarters of what a third invests. What is the ratio of the three investments, in that order?
questions.explanation: Take the third investment as 4. The second is three quarters of that, which is 3, and the first is twice the second, which is 6. So the ratio is 6 : 3 : 4. Choosing 4 for the third keeps every figure a whole number, since the fraction three quarters has a 4 underneath it.

questions.prompt: How many whole numbers from 1 to 60 are divisible by neither 2 nor 3?
questions.explanation: 30 are divisible by 2 and 20 by 3, with 10 counted in both, so 30 + 20 − 10 = 40 are divisible by at least one. That leaves 60 − 40 = 20 divisible by neither. Forgetting to add the overlap back gives 10, which double-counts the multiples of 6 as excluded twice.

questions.prompt: A machine completes any single job successfully with probability 0.9. What is the probability that it completes three jobs in a row successfully?
questions.explanation: The three jobs are independent, so the chance of all three succeeding is 0.9 × 0.9 × 0.9 = 0.73, or 72.9%. Each extra job multiplies the chance again, so a machine that is 90% reliable on one job is only 72.9% reliable across three.

questions.prompt: Which is larger: 15% of 240, or 24% of 150?
questions.explanation: 15% of 240 is 36, and 24% of 150 is 36. The two come to the same figure. That is no accident: a percentage of a number is the two multiplied and divided by 100, and 15 × 240 equals 24 × 150, so the order can be swapped freely.

questions.prompt: A tank fills in 6 hours. A leak would empty a full tank in 12 hours. The leak is open for the first 2 hours only and is then sealed. How long does filling take altogether?
questions.explanation: With the leak open the tank gains 1/6 − 1/12 = 1/12 of its volume an hour, so the first 2 hours fill 16.67% of it. The remaining 83.33% fills at the full 1/6 an hour, taking 5 hours: 7 hours in all, 1 more than if the tank had never leaked.

questions.prompt: A right-angled triangle has a hypotenuse of 26 cm and one leg of 10 cm. What is its area?
questions.explanation: The other leg is the square root of 26² − 10² = 576, which is 24 cm. The area is half the product of the two legs: 10 × 24 / 2 = 120 cm². Using the hypotenuse as though it were a leg gives 130 cm², which overstates the area because the hypotenuse is the longest side.

questions.prompt: What is the value of 97² + 2 × 97 × 3 + 3²?
questions.explanation: The expression is (97 + 3)² written out in full, so it equals 100² = 10,000. Recognising the pattern avoids squaring 97 at all — 9,409 is 97² on its own, which is the answer to a different question.

questions.prompt: What fraction of a day is a 7.5-hour shift?
questions.explanation: 7.5 hours out of 24 is 7.5/24, which doubles to 15/48 and then divides by 3 to give 5/16. 15/48 is the same number but not in its lowest terms, and 1/3 would be 8 hours rather than 7.5.

questions.prompt: What is 90 km/h in metres per second?
questions.explanation: There are 1,000 metres in a kilometre and 3,600 seconds in an hour, so multiply by 1,000 and divide by 3,600 — that is, divide by 3.6: 90 / 3.6 = 25 m/s. Multiplying by 3.6 instead gives 324, and the two conversions differ by a factor of nearly thirteen, so the direction matters.

questions.prompt: An item sells for £48.00. Its cost rises from £30.00 to £36.00 while the price is held. What is the new profit as a percentage of the selling price?
questions.explanation: The profit falls from £18.00 to £12.00, and £12.00 out of £48.00 is 25%. The margin was 37.5% before. The cost rose by 20%, but that is a change in the cost rather than the new margin.

questions.prompt: A grouped table records 40 values: 0 to 9: 5, 10 to 19: 8, 20 to 29: 12, 30 to 39: 9, 40 to 49: 6. Which class contains the median?
questions.explanation: With 40 values the median lies between the 20th and 21th. Running totals are 0 to 9: 5, 10 to 19: 13, 20 to 29: 25, 30 to 39: 34, 40 to 49: 40. The 13th value ends the 10 to 19 class, so both the 20th and 21th fall in 20 to 29. That class also has the largest frequency, but the two facts are separate.

questions.prompt: Taking pi as 22/7, a cylinder has a curved surface area of 440 cm² and a height of 10 cm. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: The curved surface is 2 pi r h, so 440 = 2 × 22/7 × r × 10, giving r = 7 cm. The volume is pi r² h = 22/7 × 7² × 10 = 1,540 cm³. 154 cm² is the area of one circular end, which is a step along the way rather than the answer.

questions.prompt: A printer charges £340.00 for 500 copies and £540.00 for 900, on the same tariff. What is the fixed charge that applies whatever the run?
questions.explanation: The extra 400 copies cost £200.00, so each copy is £0.50. The 500-copy run therefore contains £250.00 of copy charge, leaving £90.00 that does not depend on the run. Checking on the larger run: £90.00 + 900 × £0.50 = £540.00.

questions.prompt: What is the units digit of 3⁴ × 7³?
questions.explanation: The units digits of powers of 3 run 3, 9, 7, 1 and repeat, so 3⁴ ends in 1. Those of 7 run 7, 9, 3, 1, so 7³ ends in 3. Multiplying the two units digits, 1 × 3, gives 3, and only the units digits matter for the units digit of a product.

questions.prompt: A service costs £45.00 a month or £486.00 paid for a year in advance. What percentage is saved by paying annually?
questions.explanation: Twelve months at £45.00 come to £540.00, so paying annually saves £54.00 — that is £54.00 out of £540.00, or 10%. Measuring the saving against the £486.00 actually paid gives 11.11%, which answers how much more the monthly route costs.

questions.prompt: A sequence begins 50, 46, 42, falling by 4 each time. What is the first term that is negative?
questions.explanation: The terms fall by 4 from 50, reaching 2 at the 13th term and -2 at the 14th, which is the first below zero. 14 is the position of that term rather than its value — the question asks which term it is, meaning what it equals.

questions.prompt: One plan costs £1,200.00 paid at once. Another takes a deposit of £150.00 plus £95.00 a month for 12 months. How much more does the second plan cost?
questions.explanation: The second plan comes to £150.00 + 12 × £95.00 = £1,290.00, which is £90.00 more than £1,200.00. Leaving the deposit out gives £-60.00 and treats money paid at the start as though it had not been paid.
